chunks: And from him, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the 'son of the mutual imprecation' (Ibn al-La'nah), who inherits him? He said: 'His mother and the agnates of his mother.' I said: 'What do you think if his father claims him after he has already performed the imprecation with her?' He said: 'I return him to the father, because the child has no one to inherit from him (other than the father), and his mother does not become permissible to him (for marriage) until the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.يُوَارِثُهُ: He inherits from him / He is an heir to him

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a child born from Lian (mutual imprecation) and what is the status of the mother?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the child of Lian inherits from the mother and her 'asabah (agnatic relatives), as the father's claim is accepted due to the absence of another male guardian. The ruling emphasizes the permanence of the marital prohibition between the couple, rooted in the specific legal status of the child who is linked to the mother but not fully to the father. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential view on lineage and inheritance in cases of Lian, where the mother's side becomes the primary kinship network.
